slides.teacher_cue: New syllable pattern — final -le. When -le appears at the end of a word after a consonant, it makes an unstressed /əl/ sound. The e is not silent here — it combines with the l to make the syllable. apple = ap + ple. little = lit + tle. turtle = tur + tle. table = ta + ble. The consonant before -le belongs to the -le syllable, not the first syllable.
slides.expected_response: Students identify and read the -le syllable in multi-syllable words.
slides.correction_move: Model syllable splitting: ap|ple, lit|tle, tur|tle, ta|ble. Students tap the syllables. Then establish: the -le syllable is always unstressed — /əl/, not /leɪ/.
slides.observation_note: Watch for students pronouncing the e in -le as a full vowel.

slides.teacher_cue: Say apple — a fruit. ap + ple. The -le syllable is unstressed. Reveal and blend.
slides.expected_response: Students say apple orally and connect meaning before blending.
slides.correction_move: Model apple orally again, reveal and blend.
slides.observation_note: Watch for unstressed -le — not apple-ay.

slides.teacher_cue: Say little — small. lit + tle. Reveal and blend.
slides.expected_response: Students say little orally and connect meaning before blending.
slides.correction_move: Model little orally again, reveal and blend.
slides.observation_note: Watch for -tle syllable and short /ɪ/ in first syllable.

slides.teacher_cue: Say turtle — a reptile with a shell. tur + tle. r-controlled vowel in first syllable. Reveal and blend.
slides.expected_response: Students say turtle orally and connect meaning before blending.
slides.correction_move: Model turtle orally again, reveal and blend.
slides.observation_note: Watch for /ɜː/ in tur and unstressed -le.

slides.teacher_cue: Point to a table. ta + ble. Long /eɪ/ in first syllable (open syllable rule). Reveal and blend.
slides.expected_response: Students say table orally and connect meaning before blending.
slides.correction_move: Model table orally again, reveal and blend.
slides.observation_note: Watch for long /eɪ/ in ta (open syllable) and unstressed -ble.

slides.teacher_cue: Point to something purple. pur + ple. r-controlled vowel in first syllable. Reveal and blend.
slides.expected_response: Students say purple orally and connect meaning before blending.
slides.correction_move: Model purple orally again, reveal and blend.
slides.observation_note: Watch for /ɜː/ in pur (r-controlled) and unstressed -le.

slides.teacher_cue: Draw a circle. cir + cle. Soft c? No — /k/ here. ir = /ɜː/. Reveal and blend.
slides.expected_response: Students say circle orally and connect meaning before blending.
slides.correction_move: Model circle orally again, reveal and blend.
slides.observation_note: Watch for /ɜː/ in cir and hard c in -cle.
